items.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Carmen McRae, I played with her.

ctx.x: Yeah, because I like what they do. But I think when … and again I'm speaking not for the jazz community … but one of the reasons singers don't have their highest standing in the jazz instrumental community is they don't bring enough to the table. All those I spoke to … mentioned is they all play the piano. They have enough skill … Carmen McRae, I played with her. She's a great piano player, man.

items.title: Ron Carter interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

ctx.x: How did your professors feel about that? Or wasn’t it even an issue for them?

Well most of them didn’t really care. I went to class on time and did the homework. Some of them didn’t care for that kind of music so they didn’t like what I did in classes, and the school did not encourage a jazz profile. And the strange thing is at that time there was the Eastman Theater, there was a show called “Jazz for Moderns” that would travel throughout the country. And they played at the Eastman Theater, it was a wonderful auditorium, it seated maybe 2,000 people. And they had great bands going all…
force in music, it’s hard to understand how a classical institution would continue to ignore its presence.
